events.title: Great Blizzard of 1888 Begins
events.description: A massive blizzard struck the northeastern United States, dumping up to 50 inches of snow in parts of New York, Massachusetts, Connecticut, and New Jersey, with hurricane-force winds creating drifts as high as 50 feet. Over 400 people died, many in New York City.
events.significance: One of the worst blizzards in American history, it prompted New York City to bury telegraph and power lines and to build its subway system underground.

events.title: Lend-Lease Act Signed into Law
events.description: President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the Lend-Lease Act, authorizing the United States to supply Britain, China, the Soviet Union, and other Allied nations with war materiel without immediate payment.
events.significance: The act ended the pretense of strict American neutrality in World War II and made the US the 'arsenal of democracy,' greatly strengthening the Allied war effort before America formally entered the war.

events.title: Mikhail Gorbachev Becomes Soviet Leader
events.description: Mikhail Gorbachev was chosen as General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union after the death of Konstantin Chernenko, becoming the youngest Soviet leader at that time at age 54.
events.significance: Gorbachev's reforms of glasnost and perestroika transformed the USSR, helped end the Cold War, and ultimately contributed to the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991.

events.title: Tōhoku Earthquake and Tsunami
events.description: A magnitude 9.0-9.1 earthquake struck off the Pacific coast of Japan, triggering a massive tsunami that devastated coastal communities and caused the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster. Nearly 20,000 people were killed or went missing.
events.significance: The most powerful earthquake ever recorded in Japan and the worst nuclear accident since Chernobyl, it reshaped global debates on nuclear energy and disaster preparedness.

events.title: WHO Declares COVID-19 a Pandemic
events.description: The World Health Organization officially characterized the COVID-19 outbreak as a global pandemic, as the virus had spread to over 100 countries and infected more than 118,000 people.
events.significance: The declaration marked a turning point that led to widespread lockdowns, travel restrictions, and profound global social and economic disruption.
